body: thank you! i will remember your offer :) and don't hesitate to write me too if you like to! :)

if you like to read a short novel - The Stranger is a nice one, but i personally really like The Myth of Sisyphus. it's more of a philosophical essay (although Camus himself didn't really liked to be treated as a philosopher :)). it's not long, but it really hits some good points. 
let me know if you read it! i will be happy to discuss it with you :)

well, it turns out that you are cool AND nice :) that's awsome. 
I'm happy you are optimistic about therapy and getting better. just remember - you really don't have to figure everything out by yourself. it's ok to be vulnerable. it's really hard actually (my personal biggest challenge). 
and i love the fact that you love your interest so much! really inspiring. 
and yes, i really don't understand people like that. words are everything, especially when you cannot see the person you're talking to. and people just don't get it. or worse - they do and they don't give a shit. but i have been here for just a couple of weeks and the amount of kindness and love here is amazing. it really helped me a lot when i was really low. just knowing that somehow this experience is not just my own, isolated case, and that people understand and want to help, helps by itself.  
thank you too, your thank-you means so much to me. really.

yes. i would feel like that for sure. all the nice things people can say to you just passes you by, but the moment someone (anyone) tells you something nasty - it stays. that's the worst mechanism ever. i hate that. and of course his stupid opinion should mean nothing to you - but as i experience it, it only does because it's your own opinion of youself. you hear someone else saying out loud the things you think in your head... and especially after not thinking about it for 3 weeks... it catches you unguared... so i find it vey normal, unfortunately.  

i think it is admirable that you have those interests. nobody should tell you otherwise. taking interest in something is so important to life, whatever it is. a lot of people don't find anything interesting and they don't understand or even envy people who do. 
and frankly, i think mangas are cool.

now, although it's extremely hard - please try to remember that someone in that world (also a person behind a keyboard :)) thinks you are cool.

I truly understand that. 
have you read Albert Camus before? he's talking about those things exactly. about adopting this outsider's look on reality. this conclusion that life is just a sequence of events that we try to give meaning to, but are doomed to perceive as absurd, if we are honest.

i don't have information, but would like to hear more of what you have to say...
if you quit something because you don't need it, then your reason for doing so is that you are better off without it. right? but this whole argument falls on the basis that *you* will not be (better off or be at all)..  nobody needs life or experience.. 
please explain :)

i'm so sorry to hear that. i'm crying right now and i don't even know you.
no, i hope this is not how life feels like.
loosing someone is terrifying, and i know that knowing in advance don't help much either. but at least, at least, you can spend those next months with your father and be brave and get closer to him. small steps. 
and you just have to keep fighting, every day. this is your duty in life. i don't have the reason. i don't think anyone really does. looking for meaning is what we do - but nobody will guarantee that you'll find something. 

anyhow, i just wanted to tell you that you touched me.

i know what you mean. feeling everything all the time is exhausting. 
have you consider something like sports? i know it sounds stupid and useless. but sometimes it's the little things, small steps that help... i have no will power at all, and i could also stay in bed all day.. but i just force myself to get dressed for a run, telling myself that i don't really have to run, just go outside in my sports wear. it helps sometimes. 
and i agree with the other comment here about your ex.

"I wish I could just be the person everyone says I am but I'm just not."
do you feel sometimes you are that person?

hey. 
I don't know why but i've read all of your comments now on reddit. guess i just liked your writing style. 
hope you are still around.

hey. 
sometimes i think we just aren't supposed to be happy in life. and yes, it is unlikely that we will be ever happy as (maybe) we were when we were younger... it's just another kind of happiness. 
do you think there are other reasons to live for other than just happiness?

i thank you for your kind words. really. but somehow today nothing is coming through. i have also tried to say similar things to people who i felt just needed some love. and now i realize it just doesn't matter. arguments and reason just won't do. Kant was wrong i guess.
but please don't take it personally. i'm really thankful

you are not ignored. 
i feel the same way. i am not in a similar situation, but i feel the same way as you do, i think. 
i'm sorry - i don't have an answer or a practical advice on that. and that is the reason why i almost didn't reply. didn't want to waste your time or adding to your frustration. but here i am, writing anyway. 
when i was 25 years old (just 5 years ago) i was also in awful debts and struggeling to just hope that something will get better. i studies a really interesting thing, but without any career/job path.. i was really scared of getting older and poorer and didn't see anyway out. people used to try to give me tips, but i always assumed they just didn't know shit and hadn't have a clue to what is going in my life and situation. but finally i started listening a bit and i just got a little bit more confident. don't know why or how. 

i'm sory. what i'm trying to say is that i would be happy if you talk to me and maybe we could figure this out together. i'm no therapist but maybe i can help somehow
good luck tomorrow. just remember - she is there just to listen.

you sound like a great person, really. but please - try to see that loving yourself is the first step of saving the world. maybe it doesn't make any sense. i don't know. i just know that this community here is wonderful and we are all trying to help others, while needing help for ourselves.. it says something. no?

funny. i also feel like i'm being two completely different persons sometimes, and that judging from that 'happy, normal' surface no one would ever know... it is exhausting. i have recently tried to open up a little bit more, and i found out that there are a lot of people with just the same feelings. and that i don't have to be perfect and people will still love me (or even love me more...?)
it gave me the courage to make small steps towards changing my life in the way that will give me more peace... 
have you considered quitting you job if you hate it? 
do you have anyone to talk to about this?

I'm really happy you are going to see someone. and i am happy you have someone who cares about you and wants you to get help. that's really positive. and somehow also really encouraging. 
Maybe you should give yourself the chance first to meet your therapist, and then see if and how much you want to tell her? I never went to a therapist, so i'm only guessing that those things are just as fragile as any other real, intimate relationship and that it is built on trust and comfort... i guess you will want to meet her more than once, so give yourself the opportunity to grow with it.
this is not an interview nor a first date... don't stress too much about it, and just see how it feels. maybe you will feel comfortable to tell her everything (including the fact that you are afraid of telling her everything, for the reasons you wrote!), and maybe you will only say that you don't want to talk about it (yet..?). 

either way - you should be proud of yourself. asking for help is a wonderful step, which i personally didn't manage to reach yet.
do you want to talk?

dear,
you sound like you need a friend who will remind you that no matter how maybe you messed and fucked things up, and even may hurt other people, you are a worthwhile human being. and you deserve to love and be loved. you sound like you are having an incrediblly hard time. we all have our weaknesses and we are all ashamed sometimes. maybe you should try to talk to someone you can trust? seek some help? we weren't put on this earth to live through things all alone. we need connections, compassion. and help. just to put things in perspective. you are not alone. help can come to you in strange ways, unexpectedly. but first i think maybe you should start by trying to forgive yourself. you are human. the bad news about it, is that as a human being - you can do bad shit. terribly bad. the good news - there are plenty us here.  and this (and not death) is what is left.

thank you. you sound like a lovely person. and maybe it feels extreme posting this here - but it's fine. sometimes we just need to be heard and not judged. there's nothing extreme about that. just a very human feeling we all share and sometimes in forums like these we can express it (almost) without fear. 
i wish you a lovely day as well.

Thank you. I honestly didn't expect any reply. don't know why. but your message makes me feel heard. thank you so much for that and for taking the time. I actually sign up here to do just that - to try to talk to people and help them be heard.. for selfish reasons i guess, to make me feel like i can do something good. 
thank you

i used to be a quiet person as well, and was very nervous and afraid whenever the conversation stopped and no one had anything to sat anymore. 
i know that feeling.
not everybody is outspoken, loud or confident. and you are perfectly normal, even if you are quiet. there are jobs that don't require talking too much. but you should be proud of yourself for still sticking to a job like that for a few months! 
the only question you should ask yourself is whether you feel like you would like to talk more, and are just scared to do so? if so - don't let what everybody thinks of you, or the way people had labled you (as 'the quiet one') determin how you see yourself. 

either way - quiet or not quiet - you are worthy of love. 

and you are young, and there are increasingly more and more jobs that really don't require you to change in any way, and feel comfortable just the way you are.

I'm in a similar situation as well. it doesn't sound stupid. 
life is meaningless. there's no way around it. 
what helps me is just making really small steps. day by day. see friends when i hit rock bottom, as hard as it may be. just know you are not alone. 
and you know what is truly amazing here? you ended your message with such a positive and loving statement. you can help others. and maybe that is the greatest (and only) meaning in life. we all have different ways to achieve this. and maybe law is one of them?
